trust_boundaries.channel: transactional event, checkpoint, ownership and ledger stores
Hub task queue and signed delegated-step envelope
policy-gated model, retriever and tool egress

threats.title: Untrusted prompt or retrieval content changes control flow
prevention: The Hub compiles the ExecutionPlan; provider text cannot add nodes, tools, approvals or capabilities.
Retriever results require tenant-bound allowlisted source identifiers and structured output is schema validated.
Tool calls pass the authorization, policy, budget, approval and side-effect-ledger pipeline before invocation.
detection: Unknown or missing provenance and non-allowlisted tools produce stable denial reason codes.
Structured-output and plan-validation failures are visible as failed steps, never synthetic success.
audit: Record plan hash, policy version, allowed tool name, source identifiers and denial reason; never raw secrets or full prompts.
Link provider and tool observations to the canonical run and step correlation identifiers.

threats.title: A model or worker invokes an undeclared privileged tool
prevention: Allowed tools, artifacts, budgets, tenant, plan, policy, run and step are signed into a short-lived authorization envelope.
Writes require Hub revalidation, approval where declared, an ownership fence and a stable side-effect operation claim.
Workers execute one delegated step and cannot delegate or orchestrate another worker.
detection: Registry, policy, approval, budget, authorization and ledger denials stop before the invoker.
A stale fence or conflicting operation claim is rejected and an unknown outcome becomes uncertain.
audit: Record the declared operation, stable operation identifier, fence, attempt, gate and decision reason.
Record completion only after the ledger and artifact evidence agree.

threats.title: A runtime reuses Hub authority for another tenant, run or operation
prevention: Every user command and runtime envelope is bound to tenant, workflow, run, step, plan hash and policy version.
Temporal Activities submit only the signed delegated command to the internal Hub gateway; the Hub owns worker selection and task creation.
Read and command APIs derive tenant scope from the authenticated principal and use not-found semantics for cross-tenant identifiers.
detection: Any binding mismatch, missing principal, operation mismatch or stale read model fails closed with a stable reason code.
Cross-tenant read attempts do not disclose whether a run exists.
audit: Record authenticated actor, tenant scope hash, command type, plan hash and authorization decision.
Never log bearer credentials, signed envelope material or decrypted dispatch payloads.

threats.title: A command, Activity or side effect is submitted more than once
prevention: Signed commands and authorization envelopes have expiry, nonce and one-shot replay storage.
Stable operation identifiers, event dedupe keys, ownership fences and ledger CAS make duplicate delivery idempotent.
Temporal updates and signals use deterministic command identifiers and bounded retries.
detection: Nonce reuse, dedupe payload conflict, duplicate command parameters and conflicting ledger revisions are rejected.
Duplicate Temporal signals remain observable without repeating a side effect.
audit: Record a redacted command identifier, operation identifier, duplicate decision and prior ledger state.
Count retries across Temporal, Hub task, worker, tool and provider layers.

threats.title: Malformed, secret-bearing or cross-run state changes future execution
prevention: ExecutionPlan, state, event and command contracts are versioned, bounded and tenant/run scoped.
Secrets remain references; state and checkpoint serializers reject sensitive keys and arbitrary executable conditions.
Unknown schema versions are quarantined and upcasters are deterministic and pure.
detection: Schema, content hash, binding, sequence and revision validation occurs before delegation or projection.
Unknown conditions remain explicit unknown and cannot become an implicit true branch.
audit: Record schema version, content hash, quarantine reason, sequence and revision without rejected payload contents.
Preserve the original immutable event reference for forensic review.

threats.title: Modified or incomplete history/checkpoint is accepted as current
prevention: Checkpoints are signed and bound to tenant, workflow, run, task, runtime, plan, policy, revision and fencing token.
Temporal history is projected incrementally with event-id dedupe, page-loop detection, mapping version and consistency state.
A mapping upgrade requires a full deterministic rebuild before promotion.
detection: Signature mismatch, cross-runtime checkpoint, revision conflict, history gap or page-token loop makes state invalid, stale or inconsistent.
Read models never label stale or inconsistent history as current.
audit: Record checkpoint reference and digest, projection cursor, mapping version and consistency reason.
Keep raw Temporal payloads out of canonical read models; retain only protected references.

threats.title: Runtime state, provider input or UI read models disclose another tenant
prevention: Tenant scope is part of every storage key, authorization envelope, provider context and read-model query.
Provider cache keys include tenant, policy, model and prompt version; telemetry hashes tenant identifiers.
Angular receives only Hub-redacted read models and never connects to workers or Temporal directly.
detection: Cross-tenant storage, provider, projection and API reads fail closed.
Telemetry and stream payload validators reject secret-bearing or oversized shapes.
audit: Record tenant-safe correlation hashes and denied boundary, never raw credentials or cross-tenant object contents.
Record read-model staleness and evidence status so the UI cannot infer success.

threats.title: A runtime leaks credentials or unapproved data to an external provider
prevention: Provider middleware defaults external egress to deny and resolves secrets outside model-visible payloads.
Only redacted bounded request bodies reach provider transports.
detection: Egress, deadline, retry, token and cost budget violations stop before transport.
Secret-like fields are redacted before trace and event export.
audit: Record provider/model identifiers, policy decision, latency and usage, not prompt or credential content.

threats.title: The UI presents stale or unverified runtime output as successful
prevention: The UI consumes only authenticated Hub read models with explicit staleness, degradation, gaps and evidence status.
Commands require a bound approval, verified evidence and idempotency key.
detection: Completed runs without verified evidence are degraded and stale read models reject commands.
audit: Record command approval, evidence references, read-model sequence and denial reason.

threats.title: Layered retries or unbounded streams exhaust resources or repeat work
prevention: One combined retry budget covers runtime, Hub task, worker, tool and provider attempts.
Fan-out, event streams, history pages, payload sizes, Activity timeouts and heartbeats are bounded.
detection: Budget exhaustion, backpressure, history threshold and timeout uncertainty are explicit terminal or blocked states.
audit: Record consumed attempts and budget, cursor, threshold and timeout reason without content payloads.

threats.title: A leaked or miswired runtime credential impersonates the Hub or an Activity
prevention: Production Compose mounts separate Hub-private Ed25519 signing, Worker-public verification, dispatch and Hub service credentials from required external files; values never enter Compose YAML or environment variables.
Only the Hub receives authorization signing and dispatch keyrings; Native, LangGraph and Temporal workers receive public verification keys that reject private or legacy symmetric fields.

File-managed agent tokens require an absolute bounded regular file with safe write permissions, reject inline conflicts and query strings; authorization keyrings use no-follow descriptor opens, fstat validation and bounded descriptor reads; internal runtime routes require an agent service credential and reject user/admin JWTs.
detection: Missing, malformed, conflicting or unsafe credentials and verification files fail closed with a stable configuration reason; legacy shared HMAC is disabled by default.
The mandatory merged Compose-config gate proves that no Worker or Temporal service mounts Hub signing material before a production deployment.
audit: Record only the stable authentication configuration reason and affected boundary; never record the token, keyring contents or signed envelope.
Treat any Worker signing-key mount, unexpected dispatch-key consumer, accepted user JWT on an internal route or credential-bearing probe as a release-blocking boundary violation.
